topic: the concept of a chemical formula for a hydrate (water of crystallization)

easy.text: What is a hydrate, in chemistry?

options.text: A compound that has water molecules incorporated into its crystal structure
options.feedback: Correct -- hydrates include a specific, fixed number of water molecules as part of their solid structure.
A hydrate specifically refers to a SOLID compound with water built into its crystal structure, not simply any water-containing liquid.
Hydrates aren't defined as a type of acid -- they're compounds incorporating water into their solid crystal structure.

options.text: A substance that repels all water
options.feedback: This describes a hydrophobic substance, the opposite of a hydrate, which specifically incorporates water.

medium.text: The formula CuSO₄·5H₂O represents copper sulfate pentahydrate. What does the '5H₂O' part specifically indicate?

options.text: Five water molecules are incorporated into each formula unit of the crystal structure
options.feedback: Correct -- the dot notation specifically shows a fixed number of water molecules associated with each unit of the compound.

options.text: The compound is 5% water by mass
options.feedback: This notation indicates a specific whole-number count of water molecules per formula unit, not simply a percentage by mass.

options.text: The compound needs to be dissolved in 5 liters of water
options.feedback: This notation isn't an instruction for dissolving -- it describes the water already incorporated into the compound's own solid crystal structure.

options.text: The compound was created 5 years ago
options.feedback: This notation has nothing to do with age or dates -- it specifically indicates water molecules built into the crystal.

hard.text: Heating a hydrate like CuSO₄·5H₂O can drive off its water of crystallization, leaving behind anhydrous (water-free) CuSO₄, often accompanied by a visible color change. Why does removing this structural water change the compound's appearance?

options.text: The water molecules are often directly involved in the compound's crystal structure and its interaction with light, so removing them alters the arrangement and can change how the substance absorbs/reflects light
options.feedback: Correct -- hydrated copper sulfate is blue, while anhydrous copper sulfate is white/gray, precisely because the structural water's presence or absence affects the compound's light-absorbing properties.

options.text: Heating always destroys a substance's ability to have any color at all
options.feedback: Heating doesn't universally eliminate color -- in this specific case, the color change is due to the water's specific role in the compound's structure, not a general heating effect.

options.text: This color change is completely unrelated to the loss of water
options.feedback: This color change is actually directly and specifically caused by the loss of the structurally significant water of crystallization.

options.text: The compound becomes a completely different element after heating
options.feedback: The compound remains chemically copper sulfate throughout -- it's simply losing its associated water molecules, not transforming into a different element.

easy.hard: This type of compound has water molecules built directly into its solid crystalline arrangement.
easy.medium: This compound has water molecules built right into its solid structure.
easy.easy: This compound has water actually built into its solid crystal form.

medium.hard: This notation specifies a fixed, whole-number ratio of water molecules bound within the crystal lattice for every one formula unit of the compound.
medium.medium: This number tells you exactly how many water molecules are built into each unit of the crystal.
medium.easy: This tells you exactly 5 water molecules are built into each unit of the crystal.

hard.hard: The presence of coordinated water molecules can influence the electronic environment of ions within the crystal, affecting which wavelengths of light are absorbed versus reflected -- removing that water alters this interaction.
hard.medium: The water molecules are actually part of what gives the crystal its specific color, so taking them out changes how it looks.
hard.easy: The water molecules are part of what gives the crystal its blue color, so removing them changes its color.
